learningJourney.title: What are Kubernetes Workload Controllers & Services

explanation.foundation: Never deploy bare Pods—if a node dies, a standalone Pod is never rescheduled. Kubernetes manages Pod lifecycles through specialized controllers:
explanation.core:
- **Deployment**: Manages ReplicaSets for stateless, interchangeable Pods with rolling updates (`maxSurge`/`maxUnavailable`).
- **StatefulSet**: Binds stable ordinals (`pod-0`, `pod-1`) to dedicated `volumeClaimTemplates` PVCs and headless DNS (`pod-0.svc.ns.svc.cluster.local`) for databases (Postgres, Kafka, etcd).
- **DaemonSet / Job**: Runs 1 Pod per node (log/metrics agents) or run-to-completion batch tasks.
explanation.deepDive: **Services** decouple ephemeral Pod IPs via `EndpointSlice` objects programmed into kernel forwarding rules by `kube-proxy` (`iptables`/`IPVS`) or **eBPF (Cilium)**.

sectionDiagram.summary: A 10s preStop sleep gives EndpointSlices and kube-proxy time to stop routing new traffic before the app closes its socket.

learningJourney.title: Why Probe Misconfigurations & PDB Deadlocks Cause Outages

explanation.foundation: Think of **Why Probe Misconfigurations & PDB Deadlocks Cause Outages** as the intuition layer for Kubernetes Workloads & Service Routing: The problem: see what breaks without Why Probe Misconfigurations & PDB Deadlocks Cause Outages under real concurrency or scale.
explanation.core: Three operational traps cause most Kubernetes rollout outages: (1) checking downstream DB health in `livenessProbe` (if Postgres blips for 10s, kubelet restarts *every* API pod simultaneously in a cascading storm!), (2) setting a `PodDisruptionBudget` with `minAvailable: 100%` (blocking node upgrades forever), and (3) missing `preStop` sleeps causing `502 Bad Gateway` during rolling deploys.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, why probe misconfigurations & pdb deadlocks cause outages becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Kubernetes separates compute lifecycle (Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job) from stable network routing (Service + EndpointSlice + kube-proxy/eBPF) using declarative label-selector reconciliation.

ideas.title: Liveness vs. Readiness Separation
ideas.description: Check downstream DB/Redis dependencies **only** in `readinessProbe` (sheds traffic cleanly); keep `livenessProbe` strictly local (`/healthz` process deadlock check).

ideas.title: Always Leave >=1 Disruption Budget
ideas.description: Set `maxUnavailable: 1` (or `minAvailable: N - 1`) on PDBs so cluster autoscalers and node kernel upgrades can drain nodes safely.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Kubernetes Workloads & Service Routing without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When traffic spikes expose hidden coupling, match the workload controller to statefulness and scheduling needs, and pair readiness probes with PodDisruptionBudgets so zero-downtime rollouts never route traffic to unready or terminating pods.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Kubernetes Workloads & Service Routing experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: Choosing Deployment vs. StatefulSet & ClusterIP vs. Headless

explanation.foundation: Think of **Choosing Deployment vs. StatefulSet & ClusterIP vs. Headless** as the intuition layer for Kubernetes Workloads & Service Routing: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.
explanation.core: Match the controller and Service mode to your statefulness and protocol needs.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, choosing deployment vs. statefulset & clusterip vs. headless becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Kubernetes separates compute lifecycle (Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job) from stable network routing (Service + EndpointSlice + kube-proxy/eBPF) using declarative label-selector reconciliation.

benefits: Fast parallel scaling (`HPA`), interchangeable pods, and rolling `maxSurge` updates.
costs: L4 ClusterIP pins long-lived HTTP/2/gRPC connections; use L7 Envoy or Headless DNS for gRPC.

benefits: Stable ordinal DNS (`kafka-0.kafka-headless`) and dedicated per-pod PVCs for Raft/Kafka/Postgres.
costs: `OrderedReady` scales 1 pod at a time (use `Parallel` policy on 50-shard stateless/cache sets); stuck pods on lost nodes need fencing.

benefits: Deployments scale faster and avoid orphaned PVC cleanup.
costs: Ordered startup slows down HPA traffic-surge responses.

learningJourney.title: Zero-Downtime Deployment Spec: Probes, preStop & PDB

explanation.foundation: Think of **Zero-Downtime Deployment Spec: Probes, preStop & PDB** as the intuition layer for Kubernetes Workloads & Service Routing: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.
explanation.core: Combine `preStop: sleep 10`, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45`, local-only `livenessProbe`, dependency-aware `readinessProbe`, and a non-blocking `PodDisruptionBudget`.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, zero-downtime deployment spec: probes, prestop & pdb becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Kubernetes separates compute lifecycle (Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job) from stable network routing (Service + EndpointSlice + kube-proxy/eBPF) using declarative label-selector reconciliation.

learningJourney.markdownContent:
```yaml
spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45
  containers:
    - name: api
      lifecycle:
        preStop:
          exec:
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 10"]  # Wait for EndpointSlice removal
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet: { path: /readyz, port: 8080 }   # Checks DB + warmup
        periodSeconds: 5
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet: { path: /livez, port: 8080 }    # Process-local ONLY (never check DB!)
        periodSeconds: 10
```

explanation.core: Service routing implementation governs latency and rule-sync overhead at 5,000+ Services.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, alternatives: iptables vs. ipvs vs. ebpf (cilium) kube-proxy becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Kubernetes separates compute lifecycle (Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job) from stable network routing (Service + EndpointSlice + kube-proxy/eBPF) using declarative label-selector reconciliation.

benefits: Zero extra dependencies; works on every Linux kernel.
costs: `O(N)` sequential rule evaluation and full-table rewrite spikes past 5,000 Services.

benefits: `O(1)` kernel hash-table lookups and weighted/least-conn balancing.
costs: Requires `ip_vs` kernel modules and extra conntrack tuning.

benefits: `O(1)` eBPF map lookups bypassing netfilter/iptables completely, plus L7/network policy.
costs: Requires modern Linux kernel (`>= 5.10`) and Cilium CNI.
